changes.headline: Oct 1 ICE settlements: TMW front blows out $2.15 while crude rallies
changes.dek: TMW Nov26 -$23.75 (-$2.15); Dec26 -$24.25 (-$1.85, widest). The full six-contract Canadian strip settled Oct 1. WCS at Hardisty (TMW): Nov26 -$23.75 (-$2.15 on the day, 975 contracts traded), Dec26 -$24.25 (-$1.85, the widest point on the strip), then tightening about $6 into Oct27. The Jun-Oct27 tenors firmed $0.70-$1.10. WTI rallied $2.45 on the day while the TMW front blew out $2.15: WCS outright at Hardisty was $69.12, up $0.30. The weakness is 100% in the diff. WCS at Houston (ARV): Nov26 -$14.543 (-$0.771) - the Houston-Hardisty arb widened back to +$9.21 from +$7.83, so the constraint sits at the egress end, not the demand end. MSW (TMR) Nov26 -$0.1464 (+$0.85, tightening nearly a dollar); UHC (TMU) +$3.40; condensate (TMF) Nov26 +$3.8675 (+$1.12, firming into diluent season); synthetic (TMS) Nov26 +$6.29, so SYN-minus-WCS is $30.04.
changes.balance_read: The deferred heavies are not following the prompt down: this is a November-December physical crunch trading through the flat-price noise, not a structural repricing of Canadian heavy.
changes.publishers: ICE Report Center end-of-day settlements, Oct 1, 2026

changes.headline: Third carrier group, expired Iranian ultimatum, Hormuz tanker struck
changes.dek: Brent +4.4% to $102.31; WTI +2.7% to $92.87 (Oct 1 settles). The Pentagon is sending a third carrier strike group (USS Theodore Roosevelt departed San Diego Sunday; Bush and George Washington already on station) plus up to 10,000 troops, arriving by end-November. Trump told Time he expects to resume bombing Iran after the midterms. Iran's Supreme National Security Council 45-day ultimatum expired Oct 1; Fars claimed a supertanker was hit ablaze 8 km off Oman while UKMTO confirmed a tanker struck by an unidentified projectile in Hormuz - fire extinguished, crew safe. Brent settled $102.31 (+4.4%), WTI $92.87 (+2.7%), both flat in Friday Asia trade. Gulf crude exports are at 98% of pre-war (JPMorgan) and Hormuz crude at 13.5 Mb/d on the 7-day average (Kpler).
changes.balance_read: The escalation premium is earned on the supply-chain side, not the barrel side: crude flows are recovered, products are not. The $100 level is now the psychological and positioning threshold.
changes.publishers: Wall Street Journal via Business Insider; Reuters/Dow Jones; UKMTO; Al Jazeera, Oct 1-2, 2026

changes.headline: Diesel crack $101.74, eighteen straight closes above $100
changes.dek: Diesel crack $101.74 (Oct 2); 18-day streak >$100; not a record (max $117.92 Sep 16). The NYMEX diesel crack (heating oil x 42 minus WTI, front-month futures) closed at $101.74 on Oct 2 - eighteen consecutive closes above $100, the first sustained $100+ regime on record (running since Aug 17; 29 total $100+ days in the 2020+ history; pre-2026 prints were single-day expiry squeezes). Not a new record: the all-time maximum is $117.92 (Sep 16). The 3-2-1 crack stands at $67.01 against a $75.31 maximum (Aug 28). Fresh support: PetroChina canceled October gasoline/jet fuel export shipments and China froze refined product exports for October ex-Hong Kong/Macau; Ukraine struck the Volgograd Lukoil refinery (~14-15 Mt/yr) and the Samara Urals-blending station overnight; Putin acknowledged the strikes cost Russia 1% of GDP with domestic fuel queues.
changes.balance_read: The war is being fought in products now. Wide fuel margins pull refinery runs (good for barrels) but the distillate premium accrues to the upgrading barrel (bad for the diff).
changes.publishers: NYMEX front-month history, validated in-house record check

changes.headline: Pacific Link designated Canada's first project of national interest
changes.dek: Political designation, Oct 1; no prompt barrels. PM Carney and Premier Smith in Fort McMurray designated the proposed West Coast oil pipeline - now christened Pacific Link - as the first project of national interest under the Building Canada Act. About 1 Mb/d, ~1,250 km, Bruderheim to a port near Delta, B.C. on a southern route along the TMX corridor (northern coast tanker ban maintained; B.C. premier will not fight it in court). $35.2-43.7B; federal and Alberta governments 45% each, Pembina 10% (option to 20%), minimum 10% Indigenous ownership via loan guarantees. Trans Mountain Corp. leads development; conditions finalized by September 1, 2027, construction possibly starting that fall.
changes.balance_read: Long-dated and prompt-neutral, but it sits on top of Trans Mountain's own 1.19 Mb/d-by-late-2028 plan: the 2028+ egress math for Canadian heavy is improving structurally.

changes.headline: TMX drag-reducing-agent capacity +90 kbd from October
changes.dek: +90 kbd TMX capacity, starting October. Federal regulators approved Trans Mountain's drag-reducing-agent project: chemical injection skids being installed at 12 pump stations (Hinton to Hope), DRA addition commencing in October, adding about 90 kb/d of incremental system capacity. Part of the broader Mainline Optimization Program targeting 1.19 Mb/d by end-2028 (11 new pump stations, 30 km of new pipe). TMX ran at 94% utilization in Q2 (~840 kb/d); the CER toll settlement approved Sep 28 lifts firm contracted capacity from 80% to 90% of nominal from Jan 1, 2027.
changes.balance_read: Incremental egress relief lands exactly in the window the allocator's base case shows going binding: every 90 kb/d matters when the Mainline is apportioned.

changes.headline: OPEC+ meets Oct 4; consensus is a roll of November quotas
changes.dek: Expected: quotas unchanged for November. The seven core members (Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, Oman) are expected to keep November quotas unchanged at Sunday's virtual meeting. The 1.65 Mb/d of 2023 cuts were fully unwound by September; a separate ~2 Mb/d of cuts stays through end-2026. Actual supply is the constraint, not quotas: the seven core producers pumped about 25 Mb/d in August, roughly 5 Mb/d below pre-war February levels. Focus is shifting to 2027 baselines, with the DeGolyer and MacNaughton capacity assessment expected soon.
changes.balance_read: A roll is priced; the meeting only matters on a surprise. The quota architecture has been largely irrelevant since March - flows, not targets, set the price.
changes.publishers: Reuters (Wed sources); Bloomberg delegates, via Oct 1-2, 2026 reporting

changes.headline: SPR: no new DOE action; bids due Oct 6
changes.dek: RFP stands; bids due Tue Oct 6, 11:00 AM CT. No new DOE announcement Oct 1-2. The Sep 29 RFP stands: up to 40 MMbbl, all sour, 20M from Bryan Mound and 20M from Big Hill, delivery Nov-Dec 2026, minimum interest 7.5%/9.5% - far cheaper than June's 18%, which is why Sparta expects takers this time (June's round placed only ~0.5M of 40M offered). SPR at ~283.8-286.6 Mbbl, lowest since 1982; a full 40M release pushes toward the 252.4 Mbbl statutory floor.
changes.balance_read: Actual takeup is the only thing that matters. Heavy takeup displaces imported heavy/medium sour on the Gulf Coast, including the ARV leg of WCS.

changes.headline: Joliet restart still unconfirmed
changes.dek: No public confirmation as of Oct 2. The 275 kb/d ExxonMobil Joliet CDU has been shut since the Sep 13 power outage. The only restart report remains paywalled (Quantum) and unconfirmed - treat as likely restarted, not confirmed. PADD 2 gasoline at a record low (~41.8 Mbbl) against refinery runs under pressure argues for WCS demand once Joliet is actually back.
changes.balance_read: The confirmation itself is the catalyst: the discount snaps tighter when it lands, stays under pressure while it does not. Per the diff-direction rule, the outage removes a WCS buyer - the diff goes wider while offline, snaps tighter on restart.
changes.publishers: Quantum Commodity Intelligence (paywalled); ExxonMobil last public statement Sep 18

changes.headline: October Mainline apportionment: 8% lights, 4% heavies
changes.dek: Standing; November notice ~mid-Oct. October 2026 Mainline apportionment stands at 8% lights / 4% heavies (Enbridge notice Sep 16). The November notice normally lands around mid-October. The in-house allocator's base case has the Mainline going binding from November 2026, Keystone and TMX at 100%, with a max modeled congestion rent of $8.65/bbl - modeled, not observed.
changes.balance_read: October's 8%/4% is the last calm reading before the modeled squeeze; the November notice is the next real data point on this cycle.

flags.title: Joliet restart awaiting confirmation
flags.detail: Quantum headlines Joliet back in service as of about Sep 28, but the article is paywalled and no public confirmation exists. ExxonMobil's last public statement (Sep 18): power restored, restart underway, no date given. The Oct 7 EIA weekly (PADD 2 runs) is the next public test. Trigger: Public confirmation from ExxonMobil or a second source turns this into the top ranked change.

flags.title: Whiting lockout continues after failed talks
flags.detail: The Sep 29 session between BP and USW Local 7-1 failed: the union walked out without meaningfully engaging. The ~800-worker lockout (since Mar 19) continues and the strike tail stays live. Trigger: A strike authorization or walkout turns this into a ranked change; a settlement ends it.

flags.title: Synthetic crude (SCO) supply returns ~Oct 5 to mid-Oct
flags.detail: Syncrude's 50-day coker turnaround wraps around Oct 5 and CNRL's Horizon upgrader turnaround ends around mid-October. Both restore synthetic-crude supply, narrowing the synthetic-crude premium over WCS. Trigger: Confirmed completion dates on either turnaround move this into the ranked changes.

flags.title: SPR exchange bids due Oct 6
flags.detail: DOE's Sep 29 exchange RFP: 40 MMbbl all sour, Bryan Mound 20M + Big Hill 20M, delivery Nov-Dec 2026, interest 7.5%/9.5%, bids due Oct 6 11:00 AM CT. Awards are the real event; the June round took only ~0.5M bbl. Trigger: Heavy award takeup turns this into a ranked bearish change for December heavy diffs.
